objective: Make the lock header's requirements_hash checkable, so a lock regenerated before a pyproject edit cannot keep claiming a provenance it no longer has.
decision_supported: Was the stale lock in #398 detectable from the lock alone, or does something have to compare the header against the declared requirements?
acceptance: verify reports stale_requirements_hash when the header does not equal the hash recomputed from the declared requirements.
The finding names both hashes and the command that fixes it.
A lock whose header matches produces no such finding.
Editing a requirement without regenerating the lock makes verify fail with both the stale hash and the out-of-range pin.
evidence: The verifier already required the header key to be present but never compared its value, which is why #398's stale lock passed everything except the pin range check.
Changing ruff to 0.16.6 in pyproject.toml makes verify report stale_requirements_hash 897488909240... vs 25934c58a5e3... alongside the out_of_range finding; restoring it passes.
The new test rewrites only the header hash in a rendered lock and expects exactly one finding.
stop_conditions: The requirements order is not deterministic, which would make the hash unstable; locked_requirements returns the declared order and render_lock hashes that same list.
risks_and_fallbacks: A stale header is now a hard failure, so a contributor who edits pyproject must run make lock-python; the message says exactly that.
The check is skipped when the header key is absent, because a missing key is already a separate finding.
